segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר: כּוּתָּח וְכׇל מִינֵי כוּתָּח — אָסוּר לִמְכּוֹר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם קוֹדֶם לַפֶּסַח.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,» who agrees in principle with Beit Shammai’s opinion, «says:» With regard to «kutaḥ,» a dip that contains leavened breadcrumbs, «and all types of kutaḥ, it is prohibited to sell» it to a gentile «thirty days before Passover.» Because kutaḥ is spicy, people use only a bit at a time, so it will likely last until Passover.

moves.summary: kutaḥ may not be sold thirty days before Passover
moves.about: whether leaven (kutaḥ) may be sold to a gentile whenever eating it is still permitted

edges.about: whether leaven (kutaḥ) may be sold to a gentile whenever eating it is still permitted

positions.claim: kutaḥ may not be sold to a gentile within thirty days of Passover
